stem: What is start-up capital?

options.content: Finance needed to set up a new business
options.rationale: Correct: for first assets, stock and early expenses.

options.content: Profit made in the first year of trading
options.rationale: Profit is earned later, not raised to start.

options.content: Money paid to shareholders as dividends
options.rationale: Dividends are a share of profit.

options.content: Tax paid when a business is registered
options.rationale: Registration fees are only one small start-up cost.

explanation: Start-up capital pays for what a new business needs before it earns income.

stem: Which is a long-term finance need?

options.rationale: Correct: the building will be used for many years.
Wages are a short-term need.

options.content: Buying stock for the festive season
options.rationale: Stock is sold within months: short-term.
Bills are day-to-day revenue expenditure.

explanation: Long-term needs are for assets used over many years.

stem: Which is an example of capital expenditure?

options.rationale: Rent is revenue expenditure.
Fuel is a running cost.
Wages are revenue expenditure.
Correct: a non-current asset used for several years.

explanation: Capital expenditure buys non-current assets; revenue expenditure pays running costs.

stem: Why might a profitable business still need short-term finance?

options.content: Profitable businesses are not allowed to borrow
options.rationale: No such rule exists.

options.content: Its non-current assets have increased in value
options.rationale: A rise in asset value does not create a cash need.

options.content: It has too much cash in the bank
options.rationale: Too much cash does not create a need for finance.

options.content: Customers on credit have not yet paid
options.rationale: Correct: profit is not the same as cash in hand.

explanation: Timing gaps between paying suppliers and receiving cash create short-term needs.

stem: A printing business replaces a worn-out printing press. Which reason for needing finance is this?

options.rationale: The business is already trading.
Working capital is for day-to-day spending.
Correct: the old press has worn out.
Dividends are not a finance need.

explanation: Assets wear out and must be replaced to keep output and quality.

stem: A business plans to use its overdraft to buy a building. Why is this risky?

options.content: Overdraft interest is never charged on buildings
options.rationale: Interest is charged on any overdraft.

options.content: Buildings cannot be bought with borrowed money
options.rationale: Buildings are often bought with loans or mortgages.

options.content: The bank can demand the overdraft back at short notice
options.rationale: Correct: a long-term asset is financed with short-term money.

options.content: Overdrafts must be repaid in exactly one month
options.rationale: There is no fixed one-month rule.

explanation: Long-term needs should be matched with long-term finance.
hints: How long will the building be used, and how long can the overdraft be relied on?

stem: A seasonal clothing shop needs extra stock each November and sells it by January. What kind of finance need is this?

options.rationale: Stock is not a long-lasting asset.
Correct: repaid from sales within a few months.
The shop is already trading.

options.content: A need to replace non-current assets
options.rationale: Stock is a current asset.

explanation: Seasonal stock is a short-term need, financed by overdraft or trade credit.
hints: How long before the stock turns back into cash?

stem: In ZIMSEC Commerce, capital invested in buildings and machinery that stays in the business for many years is called:

options.rationale: Short-term capital finances current assets.
Correct: it finances non-current assets.
Working capital is current assets minus current liabilities.
Called-up capital relates to shares.

explanation: Long-term (fixed) capital is tied up in non-current assets.

stem:
Sipho plans a vegetable wholesale business in Mutare. His estimated start-up needs are:

| Need | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Second-hand delivery truck | 7,800 |
| Cold room for vegetables | 4,300 |
| Opening stock | 1,650 |
| Cash reserve | 900 |

Calculate the total start-up capital he needs.

Tendai is starting a transport business. He needs a minibus (US\$9,600), workshop tools (US\$2,750), spare parts to be used in the first months (US\$1,180) and a fuel float (US\$640). How much of his finance is needed for **long-term** assets?
explanation: The minibus and tools last many years: 9,600 + 2,750 = US\$12,350.
workedSolution: 1. The minibus and tools last many years: 9,600 + 2,750 = US\$12,350.
hints: Which items will still be in use in five years?

stem: A brick-making business wants a machine costing US\$6,200. It has US\$2,450 of retained profit to use. How much external finance does it need?
Paying wages is an example of revenue expenditure.
explanation: True. Wages are a day-to-day running cost.

stem: Inventory is a long-term finance need because a shop always holds some stock.
explanation: False. Each item of stock is sold and replaced within months, so it is a short-term (working capital) need.

stem: Match each situation with the reason the business needs finance.

left.content: A new hair salon buys chairs and dryers before opening
A bakery opens a second branch in another town
A transport firm replaces a lorry that has worn out
A shop pays suppliers before credit customers pay

explanation: Each stage and activity of a business creates a different need for finance.

stem: Complete the sentences.

payload.template: Spending on non-current assets such as machinery is {{blank:a}} expenditure. Spending on day-to-day costs such as rent is {{blank:b}} expenditure.

explanation: Capital expenditure buys long-lasting assets; revenue expenditure pays running costs.

stem: What is the name for the finance needed to set up a new business?
explanation: Start-up capital.

stem: Explain **two** reasons why an established business needs finance.

points.description: Reason, e.g. expansion (1)
Explained, e.g. new branches or machinery need large sums before extra sales arrive (1)
Reason, e.g. replacing assets / new technology / working capital (1)
Explained, e.g. wages and suppliers must be paid before customers pay (1)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An established business needs finance to expand, for example to open a new branch, because the cost is paid long before extra sales arrive. It also needs working capital to pay wages and suppliers while waiting for credit customers to pay.

explanation: Name each reason and explain why money is needed in advance.
hints: Think about growth and day-to-day running.

stem: Explain why a business should match the length of its finance to the length of its need.

points.description: Long-term assets earn income over many years, so repayments can be spread (1)
Short-term finance for a long-term asset may have to be repaid before the asset has earned enough (1)
Short-term needs are repaid quickly from sales, so long-term finance would cost interest for longer than needed (1)
Example, e.g. overdraft for a building risks the bank recalling it (1)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A machine earns income over many years, so it should be paid for with long-term finance whose repayments are spread over that time. If it were bought with an overdraft, the bank could demand repayment before the machine had earned enough. For short-term needs such as stock, long-term loans would mean paying interest long after the stock has been sold.

explanation: Matching avoids repayment pressure and unnecessary interest.
hints: When does an asset earn the money to repay the finance?

stem:
Nyasha plans to open a bakery in Bulawayo. Her estimated needs are:

| Need | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Commercial ovens | 5,400 |
| Shop fittings | 2,100 |
| Flour, sugar and packaging | 1,350 |
| Rent and wages for the first month | 1,800 |
| Total | 10,650 |

She has US\$4,000 of savings. Her bank has offered either an overdraft or a five-year loan.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the finance Nyasha needs in addition to her savings.

payload.template: The ovens are a {{blank:a}} need. Flour, sugar and packaging are a {{blank:b}} need.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why Nyasha needs money for the first month's rent and wages before she opens.

points.description: Expenses are paid before sales revenue comes in (1)
Sales may be slow at first while customers learn about the bakery (1)

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Recommend whether Nyasha should use the overdraft or the five-year loan for the ovens. Justify your answer.

points.description: Ovens are long-term assets used for years (1)
Loan repayments spread over five years while the ovens earn income (1)
Overdraft can be withdrawn at short notice / higher interest (1)
Justified recommendation: loan for ovens; overdraft only for short-term gaps (1)

explanation: Total needs US\$10,650; external finance US\$6,650. Long-term assets should be financed long-term.
hints: Subtract her savings from the total.
How long will the ovens last?

stem: Gweru Metalworks (a fictional sole trader) makes window frames. Orders are rising, and the owner wants to buy computer-controlled cutting equipment and a second welding machine. Some of the existing machines are old and break down often.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Identify **three** reasons why Gweru Metalworks needs finance.

points.description: Expansion / extra capacity for rising orders (1)
New technology: computer-controlled equipment (1)
Replacing old machines (1)

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State whether these needs are short-term or long-term and give a reason.

points.description: Long-term (1)
The machines will be used for many years (1)

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why the business will also need more working capital as orders rise.

points.description: More raw materials such as steel must be bought (1)
More wages to pay (1)
Customers may pay later, so cash is tied up before payment (1)

explanation: Expansion, new technology and replacement are long-term needs; rising orders also need more working capital.
hints: List what the owner wants to buy and why.
